courses.title: Entrepreneurship and Innovation (ENT 211)
courses.description: Entrepreneurship concepts, opportunity identification, business planning, financing and innovation — including health-care enterprise in Nigeria.

topics.title: Concepts of Entrepreneurship
topics.summary: Definitions, characteristics of entrepreneurs and the role of entrepreneurship in development.

material.heading: Meaning
material.body: Entrepreneurship is the process of identifying an opportunity, mobilising resources and bearing risk to create value through a new or improved product, service or organisation. The term comes from the French 'entreprendre' (to undertake). Joseph Schumpeter described the entrepreneur as an innovator who brings 'creative destruction' — new combinations that displace old ones. Richard Cantillon first used the term in economics and stressed risk-bearing.
keyPoints: Entrepreneur: identifies opportunity and bears risk

material.heading: Characteristics and importance
material.body: Successful entrepreneurs typically show need for achievement (David McClelland), calculated risk-taking, creativity, self-confidence, persistence, an internal locus of control and good networking. Entrepreneurship creates jobs, mobilises local resources, promotes innovation, reduces rural–urban migration and diversifies the economy — important for Nigeria's large youth population. Intrapreneurship is entrepreneurial behaviour within an existing organisation. Social entrepreneurship pursues social goals (e.g. affordable clinics, health apps).

topics.title: Opportunity Identification and Creativity
topics.summary: Sources of business ideas, feasibility, SWOT analysis and creativity techniques.

material.heading: Finding opportunities
material.body: Business ideas come from unmet needs, problems, hobbies and skills, changes in technology, government policy, demographic trends and gaps in existing markets (e.g. long hospital queues suggesting appointment apps, poor cold-chain suggesting solar fridges). An idea becomes an opportunity when it is attractive, durable, timely and can create value for customers. A feasibility study assesses market, technical, financial, legal and organisational viability before investment.

material.heading: Analysis and creativity
material.body: SWOT analysis examines internal Strengths and Weaknesses and external Opportunities and Threats. PESTLE analysis examines Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Legal and Environmental factors. Creativity techniques include brainstorming (generating many ideas without criticism), mind mapping and design thinking (empathise, define, ideate, prototype, test). Innovation may be incremental (improving existing products) or radical/disruptive.
keyPoints: Design thinking: empathise → define → ideate → prototype → test

questions.explanation: Opportunities and threats are external; strengths and weaknesses internal.

questions.explanation: Feasibility studies examine market, technical and financial viability.

questions.explanation: Brainstorming defers judgement to encourage creativity.

questions.explanation: Incremental innovation makes small improvements.

questions.explanation: Limited capital is an internal weakness.

options: Can create value for customers and is viable
questions.explanation: An opportunity is an idea with real market value and feasibility.

topics.title: The Business Plan and Forms of Business Ownership
topics.summary: Components of a business plan and types of business ownership in Nigeria.

material.heading: Business plan
material.body: A business plan is a written document describing a business's goals and how it will achieve them. Typical sections: executive summary (written last, read first), business description, market analysis, marketing plan (the 4 Ps — product, price, place, promotion), operations plan, management and organisation, and financial plan (start-up costs, projected income statement, cash flow and break-even analysis). It guides the entrepreneur and helps attract investors and lenders.
keyPoints: Financial plan includes cash flow and break-even

material.heading: Forms of ownership
material.body: A sole proprietorship is owned by one person — easy to start, but with unlimited liability. A partnership has 2–20 partners sharing profits and liabilities. A limited liability company (private 'Ltd' or public 'Plc') is a separate legal entity; shareholders' liability is limited to their shares. Cooperatives are owned by members for mutual benefit. In Nigeria businesses and companies are registered with the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) under the Companies and Allied Matters Act (CAMA) 2020.

questions.explanation: It summarises the whole plan, so it is written last.

questions.explanation: The owner is personally liable for all debts.

questions.stem: The law governing company registration in Nigeria is:
questions.explanation: The Companies and Allied Matters Act 2020.

topics.title: Financing, Record Keeping and Marketing
topics.summary: Sources of finance, basic bookkeeping, and marketing a small business.

material.heading: Finance
material.body: Sources of finance include personal savings, family and friends, cooperative societies and esusu/ajo rotating savings, microfinance banks, commercial bank loans, government intervention funds (e.g. Bank of Industry, SMEDAN support), grants, angel investors and venture capital (in exchange for equity), and crowdfunding. Debt financing must be repaid with interest; equity financing gives investors ownership. Working capital = current assets − current liabilities.
keyPoints: Debt: repay with interest; equity: give up ownership

material.heading: Records and marketing
material.body: Good records (cash book, sales and purchases records, inventory, receipts) help track performance, plan, pay tax and obtain loans. The income statement shows profit or loss over a period; the balance sheet shows assets, liabilities and owner's equity at a point in time (Assets = Liabilities + Equity). Marketing identifies customers' needs and satisfies them profitably; small businesses use word of mouth, social media, customer service and branding. Mixing personal and business money is a common cause of small-business failure.

questions.explanation: Equity investors receive ownership shares.

topics.title: Innovation and Entrepreneurship in Health Care
topics.summary: Innovation types, intellectual property, and health-sector business opportunities.

material.heading: Innovation and intellectual property
material.body: Innovation is the successful application of new ideas: product, process, service, business-model or social innovation. Intellectual property protects creations: patents (inventions, typically 20 years), trademarks (brand names and logos), copyright (literary and artistic works, software) and industrial designs. In Nigeria patents and trademarks are registered with the Commercial Law Department (Trademarks, Patents and Designs Registry) and copyright is administered by the Nigerian Copyright Commission.

material.heading: Health-care enterprise
material.body: Health professionals can build ventures in community pharmacy, diagnostic laboratories, imaging centres, physiotherapy clinics, home nursing, medical supplies, health insurance support, telemedicine and digital health apps. Health businesses must comply with professional regulations (e.g. PCN licensing of pharmacies, MLSCN registration of laboratories), NAFDAC product registration, and ethical standards that put patient welfare first.

questions.stem: Legal protection for a new invention is a:
questions.explanation: Patents protect inventions for about 20 years.

questions.stem: A company logo is protected by a:
questions.explanation: Trademarks protect brand names and logos.

questions.stem: Software code and textbooks are protected by:
questions.explanation: Copyright covers literary and artistic works including software.

questions.stem: Which Nigerian agency registers drugs and health products before sale?
questions.explanation: The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control.

questions.stem: A community pharmacy premises must be licensed by the:
questions.explanation: The Pharmacy Council of Nigeria licenses pharmacy premises.

questions.stem: Offering consultations by video call to rural patients is an example of:
questions.explanation: Telemedicine is a service/process innovation.

questions.stem: Changing how a clinic delivers care to cut waiting time is a:
questions.explanation: Process innovation improves how things are done.

questions.stem: The main ethical principle for health entrepreneurs is that:
options: Only the rich should be served
questions.explanation: Professional ethics require putting patient welfare first.
